sentences.text:
By means of this bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.
213 of 2023 at Police Station Bhamaura, District Bareilly under Sections 363, 376-D, 376(2)N, 506 I.P.C. and Section 5/6, 16/17 POCSO Act.
The applicant is in jail since 26.09.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 20.01.2024.

The following arguments made by Shri Lal Vijay Singh, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant,
which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Ms. Sujata Chaudhary, learned AGA from the record,
entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1.
The victim was wrongly shown as a minor of 16 years of age in the FIR only to falsely implicate the applicant under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act and cause his imprisonment.

2. Learned counsel for the applicant contests the age of the victim set out in the prosecution case in light of the judgement of this Court in Monish Vs. State of U.P.
and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021) on the following grounds:
(i) There are material contradictions in the age of the victim as recorded in various prosecution documents.

entities.text:

and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (ii) The victim in her statement under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. has asserted that she is 17 years of age.
(iii) The medical report drawn up to determine the age of the victim opines that she is around 17 years of age.
Two submissions are made in regard to the aforesaid medical report.
Firstly, the range of error in determining the age is about two years and the same should be read in favour of the applicant at this stage.
Secondly, the relevant scientific criteria as per latest medical protocol which would establish the majority of the victim has been excluded from consideration in the medical report.
The medical report is flawed.
In fact the victim is a major.
3. The victim was intimate with one Gyani.
She eloped with him to Haryana.
The couple got married in Haryana.
4. The F.I.R. is the result of opposition of the victim's family to the said relationship and to deflect attention from her conduct.
5. The applicant was not named in the FIR.

6. False and aggravated allegations were made by the victim in her statements under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. at the behest of her parents only to wreak vengeance against the entire family of her Mani Kashyap vs State Of U.P. And 03 Others on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184092747/
2 love interest Gyani.
7.

entities.text: Mani Kashyap vs State Of U.P. And 03 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The victim in the aforesaid statements has admitted that she travelled to Haryana of her own volition.
She was never confined or bound down.
She never raised an alarm.
Her conduct shows that she was a consenting party and the prosecution case against the applicant is false.
8. Further, the statements of the victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C. discloses that she was abducted from her house by three persons including the applicant.
The said persons also stole money and jewellery while they forcibly took away the victim.
9. The incident occurred in the house of the victim.
She did not raise an alarm.

The family members of the victim who were present in the house were not alerted to the presence of intruders who not only abducted the victim but also stole jewellery and other precious items which were always safely locked up in the house.
10. The prosecution story is inherently false and liable to be disbelieved.
11. Material inconsistencies in the FIR, the statements of the victim under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. discredit the prosecution case.
12. The victim was never confined or bound down in any manner.
The victim was present at various public places but never raised an alarm.
Her conduct shows that the FIR was false.
13. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
14. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
15. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of her influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Mani Kashyap be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
( ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
